evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml:5-8 functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; gates render/constraints=0.0 (lines 1-3); floor functional=0.05 (line 11). Byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml (diff empty) and score.py is identical to the template (diff empty); score.py:46-48 computes weighted mean and zeroes reward unless gates pass and functional > 0.05. Matches SKILL.md delivery profile and Internal sheet E45 ('Functionality has 60 percent'). Maximum combined non-functional contribution is 0.4 < functional 0.6, and polish/visual cannot pay at all unless functional clears the floor. No weight/model keys in any [judge] block (parsed keys: isolated, judge, mcp_servers, mode, prompt_template, timeout for all five files), so dimension weight lives only in scoring.toml. Per-criterion functional weights (scored/functional/judge.toml, 43 criteria, sum 58.5; parsed with tomllib): heaviest 2.5 on hro_stale_refused (line ~198, server-side stale-write refusal naming the changer), hro_live_board (~288, no-reload propagation), hro_candidate_private (~387, data-leak/privacy); 2.0 on all-or-none bulk, undo restore/conflict, earlier-page paging, unread counts, scrolled-up unread, drafts, refused put-back; 1.5 on server enforcement/core flows (one-stage move, reorder, full Interview, anonymous 401, bulk, threads, seen, access, candidate view, restart); 1.0 on narrower rules; 0.5 on rows that are either gate-duplicated (hro_job_open line ~27, hro_add_candidate ~36 - opening a job and adding a candidate is already required by the constraints gate hro_gate_shared) or narrow single-refusal/linking rows (hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked). Weight therefore rises with the hardness and integrity value of what is proven (server-enforced concurrency, atomicity, privacy, live sync) and falls where proof is redundant or narrow - consistent with 'weight tracks what each thing proves'. Each single functional criterion is 0.5%-2.6% of reward, so no single row dominates. Polish (0.2): 5 binary behavioural rows (live-update state preservation 3/3, earlier-page anchor 2, failed send 1.5, session resume 2.5; sum 12) - these grade real behaviour, not style, and are capped at 0.2. Visual (0.2): 5 likert(5) rows at equal 1.2 weight with anchors; pure style capped at 0.2, equal weights appropriate for parallel craft facets (Likert presence is a listed false positive). Gates carry no reward mass (all_pass, single binary criterion each). Counterfactual 1 (broken app that could win on weight): a polished, visually strong app that passes both gates but whose server enforces nothing - it can earn job_open/add_candidate/email rules (2/58.5*0.6 ~= 0.02) which is below the 0.05 floor -> reward 0; if it squeaks past the floor with a few more rows (e.g. functional 0.1), its ceiling is ~0.06 + 0.2 visual + polish rows that need working live updates (rows say 0 when no update arrives) => well below a functionally complete but plain app (>= 0.6 + likert minima). Ranking is preserved by weight. Counterfactual 2 (conforming alternative penalised by weight): an app that does everything server-side correctly but restores focus differently loses only hro_refused_put_back (2/58.5*0.6 ~= 2.1%); an app that relies on gate-proven creation loses nothing extra; no conforming design is disproportionately penalised by any single weight. Minor observations (not defects): hro_refused_put_back (weight 2, UI-focus/real-place after refusal) is weighted above hro_interview_full (1.5, the server cap itself); defensible because it also requires the card in its real stage and place and is the harder UI outcome, and the server cap is additionally exercised by hro_bulk_places (1.5) and hro_undo_full (0.5). Risk=true only because required runtime evidence is absent: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the weight analysis above is static and arithmetic, not a measured reward-ordering run. No defect found in the weights themselves.
